newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican separatist leader remanded in France.
newsitem.headline: Corsican separatist leader remanded in France.

text.p: France's top anti-terrorist judge on Wednesday ordered Corsica's best-known hardline separatist leader and his girlfriend remanded in custody and probed for attempted extortion and bomb attacks, justice sources said.

Magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere, after grilling them, formally placed Francois Santoni and Marie-Helene Mattei under investigation on suspicion of belonging to a group involved in terrorist activities, recreating a banned organisation, extortion and complicity in destruction of property by explosives.
The government ordered a crackdown after separatists stepped up attacks in a two-decade-old campaign to demand greater autonomy from Paris for the Mediterranean holiday island.
Santoni is the general secretary of Cuncolta Naziunalista, the legal party of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) Historic Wing. His girlfriend is the separatists' leading lawyer.
He surrendered to police on Monday after she was detained in connection with a bomb attack on a Corsican golf club connected with an attempt to extort "revolutionary tax".

The club's owner refused to pay four million francs ($800,000) and, in a rare act of cooperation with the police in Corsica, called in detectives after the groundsman's house was blown up last Thursday.

He alleged that Mattei had told him on her cellphone to expect the "collectors". Eight more suspects are being held in the case and French radio said another three were detained in Corsica on Tuesday night.
Santoni had been on the run since he was sentenced in his absence in October to four months in prison for carrying guns.
The FLNC has claimed a string of recent bomb attacks in Corsica and on the French mainland, including one on the mayoral office of Prime Minister Alain Juppe in Bordeaux.

The separatists have threatened "new forms" of attacks in Corsica and on the mainland. French radio said the government, fearing retaliation for the detention of Santoni, was beefing up security forces on the island with 100 riot police.
